# Segment — Free resources for startups

No startup credits are offered. Twilio, which owns Segment, states every customer gets a small account-opening credit and that no additional credits are offered to startups. The former Segment Startup Program pages now redirect to Twilio.

### Notes

This is a negative record and is likely to contradict stale third-party listings of a "$25,000 Segment Startup Program". Evidence that the Segment-branded program pages are gone: https://segment.com/industry/startups/ returns a 301 cross-domain to https://www.twilio.com/en-us/solutions/startups; https://segment.com/learn/industry/startups/ resolves through to https://segment.com/pricing which 301s to https://www.twilio.com/en-us/pricing/customer-data; and the original announcement post https://segment.com/blog/introducing-the-segment-startup-program/ 302s to https://twilio.com/en-us/partners/. The destination Twilio startups page mentions Segment only in login navigation and footer status links, with no Segment Startup Program anywhere on it. https://segment.com/docs/guides/usage-and-billing/discounts-for-startups-npos/ returned 403 to automated fetching and could not be inspected, so a residual docs-level discount for startups or nonprofits cannot be ruled out; status is recorded as no-program on the strength of the affirmative Twilio FAQ sentence, not on the redirects alone. Imported from a verification sweep whose quote fidelity later failed audit in 13 of 22 sampled records. This entry was NOT independently re-audited, so the evidence quote may be a close paraphrase rather than the vendor's exact wording. Re-read the source before relying on precise phrasing. Re-confirmed verbatim on Twilio's own FAQ 2026-09-16. This is an explicit vendor statement that no startup credits exist, which is why the record is kept rather than deleted.
